name: National Bank of Bahrain
founded: 1957 (incorporated by Amiri decree in January 1957; Bahrain's first locally owned bank)
regulators: CBB (licensed as a conventional retail bank)
ownership_summary: Listed on Bahrain Bourse (code NBB). Bahrain Mumtalakat Holding Company holds 44.06% (on behalf of the Government of Bahrain per the Bourse shareholder list) and the Social Insurance Organisation 10.85%; the remaining 45.09% is private and institutional (AR 2025, 31 Dec 2025). NBB has controlled Bahrain Islamic Bank since 2020 (80.2% at 30 Jun 2026). A non-binding MoU to explore a merger with BBK was signed on 2 Nov 2025 and negotiations on terms were still under way in Jul 2026; Group CEO Usman Ahmed's resignation (last day 31 Dec 2026) was announced on 30 Sep 2026.

government_link: Yes - Bahrain Mumtalakat Holding Company (sovereign wealth fund) 44.06% and Social Insurance Organisation 10.85% (as of 31 Dec 2025); Mumtalakat appoints four of eleven board members and SIO one (AR 2025 governance report).
group_structure: NBB Group's consolidated statements include NBB and one subsidiary, Bahrain Islamic Bank B.S.C. (BisB; 80.2% at 30 Jun 2026 vs 78.8% at 31 Dec 2025 per S3; Bahrain Bourse shareholder list shows 80.23%). BisB is profiled separately (bh-bisb): NBB's consolidated assets, deposits and profit already include BisB, so never add the two. Overseas branches in Abu Dhabi/Dubai (UAE) and Riyadh (KSA) are part of NBB itself. BBK (bh-bbk) is a separate listed bank; a potential NBB-BBK merger is under discussion (not completed at 12 Oct 2026), so BBK figures must not be added to NBB.

subsidiaries.activity: Islamic retail bank (separate CBB licence, balance sheet and brand)

footprint: Bahrain (20 branches), UAE (Abu Dhabi and Dubai branches) and KSA (Riyadh branch): 3 overseas branches; plus 7 BisB branches = 30 branches in total (31 Dec 2025). 867 employees (776 Bahrain, 40 KSA, 51 UAE) per AR 2025.
customer_segments: Retail (mass market, Prestige Banking affluent tier), Private Banking (HNW/UHNW, family offices), Strategic Accounts (ultra-high-net-worth individuals, government entities and institutional relationships), corporate, commercial and SME, financial institutions, regional (KSA, UAE).
business_lines: Retail Banking (incl. Prestige Banking, digital NBB app, Al Watani Trade brokerage); Group Corporate & Commercial Banking; Group Markets & Client Solutions (Corporate Finance, Transaction Banking, Treasury & Capital Markets incl. a dedicated Wealth Management unit and Intermediary & Custody Services); Strategic Accounts; Private Banking; Regional Banking (KSA and UAE); Islamic banking through BisB.

capabilities.wealth_summary: NBB built a wealth franchise during 2025: Treasury & Capital Markets created a dedicated Wealth Management unit (fixed income, equities, structured products, alternatives) aimed at emerging affluent and HNW clients, Private Banking got a new head (Bassam AlTattan, Sep 2025) and a digital wealth platform inside the NBB app now handles Treasury bills, government securities and sukuk. Management said ~70% of T-bill subscriptions come through digital channels, wealth revenue grew +103% y/y in Q1 2026 and structured-deposit AUM +174% y/y, and that the offer will add asset classes and explore regional expansion in 2026. Prestige Banking (affluent) lists stocks, bonds, sukuk, T-bills and structured products; Intermediary & Custody Services (bonds, sukuk, T-bills) starts at USD 200,000. Equity trading on Bahrain Bourse is offered through the Al Watani Trade app. No funds shelf, model portfolios or AUM figure was found; assets under administration were BHD 280.2m at 31 Dec 2025. The Islamic side sits in 80%-owned BisB, which has Allfunds and Societe Generale partnerships (see bh-bisb).

brokerage.detail: Al Watani Trade: online trading of stocks and other instruments directly on Bahrain Bourse (web/app; launched May 2019 per press, platform listed under Global Trading Network). Onboarding online or via branch with a minimum deposit.

digital_investing.detail: NBB Digital app: wealth management capabilities (government securities, T-bills, sukuk) launched 2025 (investor presentation dates the platform to Aug 2025; press unveiled the digital T-bills flow on 20 Oct 2025); ~70% of T-bill subscriptions now digital (Q1 2026). Al Watani Trade is a separate trading app. End-to-end digital loan origination also launched in 2025.

advisory.detail: Prestige Banking advertises 'tailored wealth management' and bespoke financial planning; Private Banking offers personalised financial planning and investment advisory; Strategic Accounts RMs promote wealth products to HNW/UHNW and public-sector clients.

discretionary.detail: Head of Private Banking oversees 'investment advisory, portfolio management and tailored financial solutions' (official bio); no discretionary mandate product or fee schedule found.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: No model portfolios or robo-advisory found on NBB pages or in AR 2025/Q1 2026 materials.

funds_platform.detail: No third-party mutual-fund shelf or platform provider found for NBB (Prestige/Private pages list stocks, bonds, sukuk, T-bills, structured products, alternatives). BisB (subsidiary) partnered with Allfunds in 2025.

structured_products.detail: Prestige Banking page lists 'Structured Products Offering: capital protection and growth'; AR 2025 says the Wealth Management unit offers structured products; Q1 2026 deck cites structured-deposit AUM +174% y/y. Issuer/manufacturer not named.

private_markets.detail: AR 2025 lists 'alternative investments' within the wealth unit's product suite and the Private Banking page mentions 'alternatives'; no named funds or platforms found.

islamic_wealth.detail: Sukuk access via NBB Digital and Intermediary & Custody Services; Shariah-compliant investing sits mainly in BisB (80.2%-owned): Islamic credit-linked note, Allfunds-based Shariah fund access.

partners.what: Al Watani Trade login is hosted on watanitrade.globaltradingnetwork.com (link on NBB site) and the App Store listing names GTN as developer (search result); exact role not described.
Press at launch (May 2019) says Al Watani Trade was developed with Mubasher / 'Bahrain Trade'; current relationship not confirmed.

partners.partner: Bank of London and The Middle East (BLME)
partners.what: Strategic collaboration giving eligible NBB HNW clients access to UK residential, investment and buy-to-let financing; signed at NBB HQ.
First bank in Bahrain to adopt the national eKey for digital onboarding (2025).
NBB website links an Open Banking developer portal hosted on tarabutgateway.io (sandbox); AR 2025 mentions open-banking participation.

initiatives.what: Digital wealth platform launched in NBB Digital (date from Q1 2026 investor presentation; press unveiled the digital T-bills flow on 20 Oct 2025).
Yusuf Ahmed Abdulla named head of Prestige Banking (press).
Bassam AlTattan appointed Head of Private Banking.
Upgraded fixed-income offer: stronger bond/sukuk market-making and expanded custody for institutional and individual clients (press).
Non-binding MoU with Bank of Bahrain and Kuwait (BBK) to start reciprocal due diligence and negotiate terms of a potential merger.
Husain Almohri takes over Group Chief Executive - Markets & Client Solutions (announced 18 Nov 2025).
NBB and BBK stated they were continuing their reciprocal due diligence for the potential merger; at BBK's AGM (31 Mar 2026) its CEO said completion in 2026 was still possible (press).
NBB submitted a proposal to BBK on key merger terms including the exchange ratio; negotiations followed. BBK said on 21 Jul 2026 discussions are continuing.
Collaboration with BLME for UK Shariah property finance for HNW clients (press, search result only).
Q1 2026 call: wealth revenue +103% y/y, structured-deposit AUM +174%, ~70% of T-bill subscriptions digital; wealth offer to add asset classes in 2026 and explore regional expansion.

H1 2026 results: record Q2 attributable profit BHD 22.5m, H1 BHD 43.1m; interim dividend 10 fils proposed; management cites 124 promotions and a joint lead manager role on Bahrain's USD 1bn 10-year bond.
Resignation of Group CEO Usman Ahmed announced (last day 31 Dec 2026); board running a search with an independent executive-search firm; merger said to continue on its own timeline.

opportunities: Management plans to widen the digital wealth platform to additional asset classes in 2026 and to explore regional expansion; wealth is described as a key driver of fee-income growth in 2026 (S6 p.3, S7 p.3).
Wealth Management revenue +103% y/y in Q1 2026 from a business launched in 2025, targeting emerging-affluent and HNW clients through digital capabilities (S4 p.10, S7).
Current shelf evidenced on NBB pages is stocks, bonds, sukuk, T-bills and structured products; no funds platform, model portfolios or discretionary offer was found (S16-S18).
Private Banking is exploring third-party solutions (trust/company formation, UK property and mortgage arrangements) - a pattern of sourcing products from partners (S4 p.10, S27).
barriers: Group CEO Usman Ahmed resigned (last day 31 Dec 2026) with no successor named at 12 Oct 2026 (S14, S15).
Potential merger with BBK under negotiation since Nov 2025; platform and vendor decisions for the combined bank are uncertain (S10, S12, S13).
Wealth proposition is new and fixed-income led, built by the Treasury & Capital Markets unit rather than a separate asset-management arm (S4 p.10).
Islamic wealth is housed in BisB, which has its own partners (Allfunds, Societe Generale) (see bh-bisb).
incumbent_vendors: Global Trading Network - Al Watani Trade platform (login domain and App Store developer listing; role not confirmed) (S20, S26)
Mubasher Financial Services - developed Al Watani Trade at launch in 2019 per press; current role unconfirmed (S26)

discrepancies.detail: Audited AR 2025: BHD 3,966.2m; the 30 Jun 2026 interim statements show the 31 Dec 2025 comparative as BHD 4,015.5m (due to banks BHD 894.7m vs 941.2m audited; interest payable and other liabilities 157.0 vs 159.8) - a re-presentation, total assets unchanged at 6,276.6.
discrepancies.resolution: Audited figure recorded as the 31 Dec 2025 value; 30 Jun 2026 growth vs Dec (12% per management, S5) uses the re-presented base.

discrepancies.detail: Note 30 of the 2025 accounts is titled 'Assets under management' but its text reports 'assets under administration' of BHD 280.2m.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as aua only; AUM left undisclosed.

discrepancies.detail: Q1 2026 investor presentation says 'since its August 2025 launch'; press (GDN 20 Oct 2025) describes the digital T-bills platform as unveiled in Oct 2025.
discrepancies.resolution: Both recorded; Aug 2025 (issuer) preferred for platform launch, Oct 2025 for the public T-bills announcement.

discrepancies.detail: NBB fully consolidates BisB (80.2%); NBB's total assets/deposits/profit include BisB's.
discrepancies.resolution: bh-bisb has parent_id bh-nbb; never add BisB to NBB group totals.

discrepancies.detail: NBB and BBK are separate listed banks; a merger is only under negotiation (MoU 2 Nov 2025).
discrepancies.resolution: Treat as independent institutions until a binding agreement and approvals are announced.

discrepancies.field: Usman Ahmed - departure from NBB vs start at Al Rayan
discrepancies.detail: NBB (GDN 1 Oct 2026) says he steps down 'to pursue a new professional opportunity' with a final day of 31 Dec 2026 and does not name the next employer; Al Rayan Bank (Al Raya, 30 Sep 2026) says he is its new Group CEO, approved by Qatar Central Bank, to start after completing onboarding, with an acting Group CEO from 1 Oct 2026.
discrepancies.resolution: Not a conflict, but his actual start date at Al Rayan is unpublished; NBB's stated final day (31 Dec 2026) is used for the NBB role and he stays 'Verified current' until then.

discrepancies.field: Hala Yateem - date she became Chairperson
discrepancies.detail: NBB's page gives only 'Joined the Board on March 2018'; AR 2023 shows her as Director with Farouk Almoayyed as Chairman; the Daily Tribune of 19 Aug 2024 reports her election as Chairperson; AR 2025 says the board was elected in March 2024.
discrepancies.resolution: Recorded as 2024 (after the March 2024 OGM, before 19 Aug 2024); exact date unresolved.

discrepancies.detail: NBB's page: BSc Business Administration (New York Institute of Technology) and Associate Diploma in Business Management (University of Bahrain); BisB's page and GDN 18 Nov 2025: BSc in Management and diplomas in business management/commercial studies (GDN: commercial studies and business administration).
discrepancies.resolution: NBB's own page wording kept in this file; BisB's wording is logged in bh-bisb.

open_items: Group CEO resignation (announced 30 Sep 2026): the Bahrain Bourse announcement itself was not opened (Cloudflare verification page). GDN 1 Oct 2026 and the Al Raya report of Al Rayan Bank's 30 Sep 2026 announcement were opened on 2026-10-13. No NBB successor was named by 13 Oct 2026 (NBB newsroom feed to 6 Oct, GDN to 12 Oct). Re-check for the successor, for the 1 Oct 2026 'Extraordinary Items' board-meeting result and the 23 Aug / 23 Sep 2026 material-information notices (titles only seen), and again after 31 Dec 2026.
Merger status after 21 Jul 2026 not confirmed: no definitive agreement, exchange ratio or timetable was found; BBK's 21 Jun 2026 disclosure was not read.
Q3 2026 results not yet published at 12 Oct 2026; add when available.
AUM, wealth client assets, customer counts and investing-user numbers not disclosed; only growth rates for wealth revenue and structured-deposit AUM.

Head of Wealth Management (Ali Janahi) and Head of Prestige Banking (Yusuf Ahmed Abdulla) rest on single 2025 press reports and stay 'Requires verification': neither is on the official leadership page, the Bourse key-persons list or AR 2025. Head of Retail Digital Banking (Omar Al Adhami) is now confirmed by the Bourse key-persons list as well.

LinkedIn: only Usman Ahmed verified (search-result match); profile searches for Bassam AlTattan and Ali Janahi returned no match; Husain Almohri and Razi Amin were not searched. No LinkedIn search was possible in the X25 pass (WebSearch quota used up after five role-based news searches).

Exact dates of Hala Yateem's election as Chairperson and of Yusuf Alireza becoming Vice Chairperson are not published in the sources opened (both after the March 2024 board election; Yateem by 19 Aug 2024).

NBB's wealth platform vendor (digital wealth module, structured products manufacturers) is not named in any source; Global Trading Network/Mubasher links for Al Watani Trade are inferred from a login domain, an App Store listing and 2019 press.
The NBB-BLME partnership (Apr 2026) was seen only in search results (article pages not opened).
Lead check (prompt: 'Mumtalakat and others'): confirmed Mumtalakat 44.06% and SIO 10.85% at 31 Dec 2025.

Not profiled (not decision-maker roles; all on the official leadership page or AR 2025 lists): Nabeel Mustafa (Acting Group COO), Hend Mohamed Mahmood (Group CHRO), Gaby El Hakim (Group Chief Legal Officer), Rana Qambar (Group Chief Compliance Officer; also a BisB director), Fadhel Abbas Ahmed (Group Chief Internal Auditor), Ali Ehsan (Group CRO; profiled in bh-bisb), Hisham Abu Alfateh (Chief Corporate Communications Officer), country CEOs Mansour A. Alsaghayer (KSA) and Yogesh Kale (UAE; NBB branches, not subsidiaries), Group Head Treasury & ALM Ali Al-Moulani, Head of Capital Market Trading Husain Askar, Group Head of Transaction Banking Vineet Munot, and the nine other directors (Sh. Rashed Bin Salman Al Khalifa, Rishi Kapoor, Vincent Van Den Boogert, Zaid Khalid Abdulrahman, Dr Paul David Pester, Isa Hasan Maseeh, Mohamed Farouk Almoayyed, Ahmed Fawzi Kanoo, Alaa Abdulkhaleq Saeed).

Leadership could change further: the Group CEO leaves on 31 Dec 2026 and the proposed NBB-BBK merger is still pending (GDN 1 Oct 2026: it 'continues to progress on its own timeline'); re-run the people check once a successor is named or the merger completes.
